absent: Definition and locking of the shared flag set-clear helper and region array growth.
Implementations of search, isolate, remove-range, remove-region and size-capping helpers.
Implementations of internal alloc, range search, flag choice, direction query, reservation and preparation helpers.
Definitions of node helpers, region node and attribute predicates, and physical memory size query.
Concurrency rules for mutation of memory and reserved collections during boot.
Numeric values and bit layout of flags, limits, sentinels and page orders.
Behavior of buddy handover, accounting, deferred page init, frame conversion and tag helpers.

findings.text: Early boot flag management offers separate set and clear operations for no-map marking on the memory collection, no-init and kernel markings on the reserved collection, and scratch marking on the memory collection. Each takes a physical base and length, delegates to a shared flag helper, reports status, and is restricted to initialization time.

Range enumeration is provided in forward subtraction form, reverse subtraction form, and page frame form over the memory collection. Callers supply a cursor with optional node and attribute filters and receive start, end and node outputs with defined terminal encodings.

Boot allocation entry points cover physical range allocation with alignment and bounds, raw node-aware allocation with strict versus best-effort node handling, huge page allocation with node preference control, and a mandatory allocation wrapper that terminates the boot on failure.

Accounting queries expose total reserved size, reserved size filtered by huge or kernel attributes with address limit truncation and node filtering, and an estimate of free pages derived from physical memory size minus kernel-reserved size.

Memory shaping operations enforce a total size limit by truncating both collections, cap the usable interval while preserving no-map entries and truncating outside reservations, remove mapping above a limit, inward-align trim extents with removal of emptied ones, and get or set a current allocation limit.

Membership tests answer whether an address lies in the reserved or memory collections, whether it lies in mapped memory by checking the no-map attribute, and whether a whole interval is covered by one memory extent after size capping.

Boot to buddy handover moves address ranges into the page allocator in maximal aligned blocks, initializes reserved descriptors as reserved, releases unused map gaps between ordered banks with pageblock rounding, and routes through a deferred-init and tag-clear gate before core freeing.

Iteration filtering never skips when the scanned collection is not the memory collection. For memory it enforces node equality when a valid node is requested and independently honors hotplug, mirror, no-map, driver-managed and scratch attributes against caller flags, skipping non-matching extents.

Forward enumeration walks the first collection in order and for each extent examines gaps preceding reservations in the second collection. It yields the overlap of extent and gap, advances the side ending first, packs both indexes into one cursor word, and writes a maximal terminal when exhausted. Without a second collection it yields whole extents.

Reverse enumeration initializes from collection ends when given the terminal sentinel, then walks downward yielding overlap of extent and preceding-reservation gap. It applies the same attribute filtering, advances the side starting later, packs indexes into one cursor, and terminates with the maximal value.

Page frame enumeration steps the memory collection in order, discards extents vanishing after upward base and downward end rounding, enforces node match when requested, and reports rounded frame bounds plus node. Exhaustion is signaled with a negative index.

Huge page boot allocation drops mirror preference, seeks an accessible range aligned to request size, optionally widens from a specific node to any node on failure with bounds reset, rejects candidates overlapping scratch by moving one bound according to allocation direction and retrying, then reserves with kernel plus huge attributes and prepares the range.

Size limits convert to a cutoff address by consuming extents in order until the budget falls inside one extent. If the budget exceeds total memory the cutoff stays maximal and nothing is truncated. Capping isolates the wanted interval, removes mapped extents outside it from both ends, and truncates outside reservations.
Trimming rounds each memory extent inward to the requested alignment, updating extents that remain non-empty and removing extents that collapse, adjusting the scan position to account for removal.

Core freeing normalizes descriptor state before buddy handover: it clears offline or reserved marking according to hotplug versus early context, zeroes reference counts, adjusts managed counts through distinct paths per context, handles unaccepted memory by queueing or accepting, and queues directly to the tail bypassing per-cpu caches.

Two build variants exist for unaccepted memory. One performs range containment checks and conditional lazy queueing, reporting whether queueing absorbed the block. The other reports no unaccepted content and treats queueing as unreachable.

Deferred descriptor initialization has two variants: one treating pages beyond a per-node deferred threshold on online nodes as not yet initialized, and one always reporting initialized. The boot free gate skips not-yet-initialized pages.

Reserved range initialization walks valid frames, runs deferred initialization, then marks descriptors reserved without atomicity because they are not yet visible. Frame interval freeing repeatedly selects the largest order allowed by alignment and remainder capped by maximum order, with explicit maximum order for zero start, and clamps high addresses when high memory is unavailable.

The unaccepted queue update is protected by the zone lock taken with interrupt state saved, covering list linkage, free page accounting, unaccepted counter update and descriptor marking, with restore on release.
A region carries a base address, a length, flag bits and node association retrievable via a helper. A collection carries a count, an array of regions, a total size and a name used in diagnostics.

A zone exposes a lock, an unaccepted list head and accounting state. A page descriptor exposes a list node used for the unaccepted queue plus state for reserved, offline and unaccepted, with reference count and zone linkage.

Global boot memory state holds memory and reserved collections, a current allocation limit, a resize permission flag and a debug flag. Dumping prints counts and per-region base, end, length, node and flags when debugging is enabled, plus aggregate sizes.

Forward cursor lifecycle: caller starts with zeroed packed indexes, each call returns one gap-clipped interval and an updated cursor preserving the untouched side index, and exhaustion stores the all-ones terminal that must not be advanced further.

Reverse cursor lifecycle: caller starts with the all-ones sentinel, callee initializes to last indexes, each call returns one interval moving downward, and exhaustion restores the sentinel to signal completion.

Huge allocation moves through search, node widening, scratch overlap adjustment and reserve-or-fail states. Node widening resets bounds to the full accessible window, while scratch overlap narrows one bound based on direction before re-searching.
Boot configuration entry points allow enabling array resizing once, toggling debug output via a command line keyword, and emitting aggregate plus per-region diagnostics during initialization.

Hazards include cursor sentinel reuse where the terminal value doubles as reverse-start trigger, limit conversion that must not truncate when budget exceeds total, scratch overlap retries depending on allocation direction, zero-start alignment edge requiring explicit maximum order, and non-atomic descriptor marking safe only before visibility.

Observed ABI facts include distinct flag bits for hotplug, mirror, no-map, driver-managed, scratch, no-init, kernel and huge reservations, node wildcard and validity concepts, maximal physical and integer sentinels, accessible and anywhere allocation bounds, pageblock and section alignment, and early versus hotplug init contexts with tail placement.
